status: PROPOSALS ONLY. No label, work order, item or AO plan was changed.
method: Eight independent read-only passes (one per author script; topic 3 split by group) read every item against its prompt, answer, guidance and planned AO demand, applying the operator-settled AO rules in planning/ao_operator_review.json. Reviewers proposed a change only when confident and listed boundary cases they kept. This is one reviewer per item, not a teacher panel.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Calculate two square areas and state the scale factor between them (4).
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Mostly routine calculation (Apply), but relating the area factor to the doubled side is a small relational step that can support Analyse.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; would move to Apply if the operator accepts the 002-group changes and wants consistency.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Write 0.0007 m as 7 x 10^-4 m and say the length is positive despite the negative power.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The conversion is Apply, but the second mark targets a misconception about negative indices, which is closer to Understand. Neither is clearly better than Analyse is clearly wrong, so keep.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; Apply or Understand would both be acceptable.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Draw a two-line graph from supplied readings, choosing axes and scales and labelling the lines.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Plotting is usually Apply, but choosing the axes and scales yourself and deciding between a line and a curve from the pattern supports Analyse. AO3 (C3) is correct.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; Apply would also be defensible.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Identify the independent variable for the x-axis, choose scales, plot three points, draw a smooth curve and add a title.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Same as 039: choosing the variable placement, scale and curve shape gives some analytic demand. AO3 is correct.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; Apply defensible.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Explain, using the 4x area and 8x volume scaling, why doubling a cube's side halves its surface area to volume ratio.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: If learners have rehearsed the SA:V doubling argument, this is a taught explanation (A1). Working out the scale factors and the ratio change is a B3/B5 reasoning step. The guidance credits that working, so B is defensible.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; would move to AO1 if the unit notes teach this exact doubling result as a fact to recall.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Describe using a ruler and set square to draw perpendicular axes.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Describing how to use an instrument fits both A3 (techniques of operation) and C1 (knowledge of how to use apparatus). Under the C1 reading and the practical-skills objective, AO3 is defensible.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; AO1 (A3) if the operator reads apparatus-use descriptions without an investigation as A.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Explain why mouth pipetting is unsafe and name the pipette filler as the alternative.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Safety knowledge of apparatus fits both A3 (aspects of safety) and C1 (using apparatus safely). The objective is a practical-handling one, so AO3 is kept.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; AO1 (A3) is the alternative reading.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Name the stopwatch as the apparatus for timing from mixing to an endpoint.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Naming an instrument is recall that fits A3 (scientific instruments) as well as C1. AO3 follows the Paper 3 objective. Bloom is really Remember, but this is a one-mark naming card with Understand as the PROC default, so the Bloom label is not pressed.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; AO1 plus Remember would be the alternative if apparatus naming is treated as A3. Same for 084, 086 and 088.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Name a thermometer or probe for checking water-bath temperature.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Same A3/C1 boundary as 082; instrument recall in a practical setting.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; see 082.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Name a balance as the apparatus for measuring mass after taring.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Same A3/C1 boundary as 082.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; see 082.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Name a burette from the description of subtracting initial and final readings.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Same A3/C1 boundary as 082. Linking the reading method to the burette asks a little more than plain recall.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; see 082.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Describe the iodine test for starch and its positive colour.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The objective is literally 'recall of simple chemical tests', which is A1/A3 knowledge. The syllabus places it among the practical skills (C1/C2 procedure and observation), so AO3 is defensible.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium-high; AO1 is the stronger reading if the operator does not count recalling a standard test procedure as a C demand.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Predict more germination on moist than dry paper because seeds need water.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The reasoning is taught knowledge (germination needs water: A1), stated as a prediction (B6), inside a planning objective (C). AO3 follows the planning context; the cognitive content is close to A.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; AO1 if the operator judges that a prediction resting entirely on taught recall is not a C demand.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Calculate magnification as 24 / 0.6 = x40 from supplied drawing and actual lengths.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The learner does not make the drawing or measure it, so the task is B3 manipulation of supplied numbers, like the AO2 CALC cards. The objective is a Paper 3 drawing skill, which supports keeping C.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; AO2 if the operator classifies by actual processing over objective placement; AO3 is more secure if the card used the learner's own drawing measurement.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Describe the trend in four supplied shoot lengths, quoting interval gains, and say growth slows then stops.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Identifying a trend from supplied data is B4, but the objective 'discuss trends in results' is the C4 practical one and the data are investigation results, so AO3 holds. 'Discuss' fits a developed account of the trend.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: low-medium; AO2 (B4) is the alternative if the data were not presented as the learner's investigation results.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Twelve multiple-choice questions: eight on practical conventions (variables, headings, error type, axes, apparatus, drawing, observation, parallax) and four on supplied-number processing.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Most stems test practical-skills content, which would point to AO3. As MCQ recognition, though, they are A (A2/A3 conventions and apparatus), and Paper 1 tests A and B only, so AO1+AO2 is consistent. Q9-Q12 are B3.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; adding AO3 would be arguable only if the set is not modelled on Paper 1.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: From supplied germination counts: name the two variables, calculate a percentage, describe the trend with values, and explain why extrapolation to 12 h is unsupported.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Parts (a), (b) and (e) touch C-type content (variables, limits of a conclusion), but as a Paper 2-style structured question the A (variable definitions) plus B (B3 calculation, B4 trend, B6 limits of prediction) labels are defensible. 'State' describes only (a) and (b), which is normal for a multi-part item.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; AO3 could be added if the task is meant to rehearse Paper 3 rather than Paper 2.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Give one taught argument for and two taught arguments against classifying viruses as living; no overall judgement is credited.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: AO1 is an operator-settled generic taught EVAL slot and must be kept. Bloom Evaluate is borderline because the guidance says no mark goes to the overall judgement, so the marked demand is recalling arguments (Understand). Weighing for and against is still defensible as Evaluate.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; if a judgement mark were added, Evaluate would be clearly right. As written, Understand would also be defensible.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Use the taught arthropod group features to reclassify a described animal (5 leg pairs, 2 antenna pairs) as a crustacean and state the insect features the error ignores.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: This matches the taught feature list for crustaceans and insects directly, so A is defensible. Assigning a described specimen to a group is a small application step that could be argued as B4 inference.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; if the workspace counts placing a described specimen in a group as B (as P01 Q9 does under AO2), this would move to AO2/Apply.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Work through a field-sampling investigation: identify variables, calculate means, describe the comparison, name a control variable, evaluate sampling bias with an improvement, then name one arthropod's group.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Parts (a) to (e) (9 of 10 marks) are investigation demands, so AO3 is correct and Evaluate fits part (e). Part (f) (1 mark) is classification from features (AO1/AO2) and is not practical. 'identify' describes only part (a), but each part carries its own command word, so no change is proposed.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: low for AO3 overall; adding AO1 for part (f) would be defensible if the workspace tags AO per mark. A command-word change would affect tariff rules, so none is proposed.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Judge a learner's conclusion from a comparison where temperature and shaking both changed, and explain why it is not justified.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: B5 (reasoned explanation in a new situation) fits. So does C5/C4 (evaluating whether a comparison controls variables), because the flaw is an uncontrolled variable. The objective is not a practical one, so B is reasonable. Evaluate would also be a defensible Bloom label for judging a conclusion.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium: would move to AO3 and Evaluate if the operator treats every uncontrolled-variable critique as method evaluation regardless of the objective.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Subtract the supplied concentrations to compare two gradients (6 vs 2 units) and state which has faster net diffusion.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The processing is minimal (one subtraction) and the conclusion is the taught gradient rule, which is near the 'a table alone does not make it B' boundary. It still needs the supplied numbers to be turned into a gradient comparison (B3/B4), so B is defensible.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium: would move to AO1 if the operator judges trivial arithmetic on supplied values insufficient for B.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Explain observed firmness and softness of pumpkin strips after soaking in water and in sugar solution using osmosis and turgor.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The explanation is the taught osmosis and turgor account (A1), but it is applied to practical observations, which is C4. C is defensible given the practical objective.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium: would move to AO1 if the operator requires processing of observations or data, not just an observed outcome, for C4.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Infer from supplied gain or loss results that the cell-content concentration lies between 0.1 and 0.2 mol/dm3, and justify it.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: AO3 (C4 conclusion from data) is right. On Bloom, Analyse (interpreting a results pattern) and Apply (applying the no-net-change principle) are both defensible.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: low on AO; medium on Bloom: Analyse would be preferred if the 3-151 Bloom change is accepted, for consistency.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Explain mineral deficiency in flooded maize by linking low soil oxygen to less respiration and less active transport.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: This is a reasoned explanation of a field situation (B5/B7). However, the taught CHAIN answer for 3-169 already states that waterlogged soil lacking oxygen reduces uptake, so the item is close to rehearsed A content.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium: would move to AO1 if learners are taught the flooding example explicitly. It stays B if 3-169 is the only place it appears and the item needs the link to be built.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Link many mitochondria in villus cells to active uptake of glucose needing respiratory energy.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: AO1 is defensible because the link is taught: 3-171's answer states that these cells have many mitochondria because active transport needs energy. This contrasts with the sibling 3-135 (AO2), where the learner must infer which unfamiliar cell does more work.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: low-medium: would move to AO2 only if the villus-mitochondria link is not part of taught content.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Explain why an enzyme acts on substrate P but not Q (similar size, different binding shape) using active-site fit.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Most of the answer is taught specificity (lock and key), which is A. The 'similar size but different shape' twist asks the learner to separate size from shape, a small piece of reasoning that keeps B defensible.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium: would move to AO1 if the operator views fit and specificity applied to labelled substrates as a rehearsed account.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Explain why a powder removing a protein stain does not show it removes an oily stain equally well, using enzyme specificity.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The content is taught specificity (protease vs lipase), which is A. It is framed as limiting a conclusion drawn from an investigation result (C4/C5), so C is defensible.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium: would move to AO1 if the operator wants C reserved for items that process method details or data.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Process supplied mean root lengths from a controlled phosphate-deficiency investigation (calculate the 4.8 cm difference) and state and explain the supported conclusion.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The demand (quote the difference in means from a controlled investigation and draw a conclusion) is structurally the same as 3-242 and 3-261, which are labelled AO3 as interpretation of investigation results (C4). B is defensible because the second mark asks for a reasoned explanation using DNA/ATP knowledge (B5), so keep, but the inconsistency with 3-242 should be noted.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; if the operator wants all 'conclusion from a controlled investigation' items treated as C, this would move to AO3 for consistency with 3-242.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Use described seedling results (iron added at week 2, plants turn green versus pale matched controls) to judge which treatment is supported and link it to chlorophyll formation.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Interpreting the outcome of a controlled treatment comparison sits on the B4/B5 versus C4 boundary (drawing conclusions from investigation results). B is defensible because the learner must infer cause from supplied information and explain it, so keep.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; a consistent rule that investigation-result conclusions are C would move it to AO3.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Apply limiting-factor reasoning to explain why CO2 enrichment raises photosynthesis in a well-lit greenhouse but not a dim one.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Greenhouse CO2 enrichment and limiting factors are taught content (A4), so A is defensible; the two-situation contrast does call for applying the limiting-factor idea, which makes AO2/Apply a reasonable alternative.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; if the dim versus well-lit contrast is judged to be a new situation rather than a rehearsed one, AO2/Apply would fit better.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Explain why equal energy needs do not imply equal iron needs when one adult has menstrual blood loss.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The reasoning (energy and iron are separate needs; blood loss removes haemoglobin iron) is close to the taught CHAIN account in 3-289, and its first guidance point is almost word for word the same as 3-306, which is labelled AO1. Separating two needs in a matched-comparison scenario is a defensible B inference, so keep.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; if the operator judges the matched-adult framing to be taught reproduction, AO1/Understand would match 3-306.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Explain why enough food energy does not prevent scurvy: energy and vitamin C are different nutrients.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: This is a taught distinction (energy versus micronutrient, scurvy cause), so A is right; it is listed only because it shares its reasoning with 3-290 (AO2), and the two labels should be read together.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: low for AO1; only relevant if 3-290 is relabelled.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Infer that changing to seated duties with unchanged intake causes an energy surplus stored as fat.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The energy-balance account is taught (compare 3-304 WHY, AO1), but the learner must infer the change in expenditure from the job change and link it to unchanged intake over time, which is a modest B7 everyday problem. Keep.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium; a reviewer who sees this as a rehearsed energy-balance account would label it AO1/Understand.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Give the taught account of why maternal milk antibodies protect a young infant temporarily.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Operator-documented breastfeeding boundary (CHAIN A provisional); the prompt is a taught passive-immunity account, consistent with A.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: low: recorded operator boundary; not proposed for change.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Use the supplied group comparison (similar exposure, similar own antibody production) to attribute fewer intestinal infections to milk antibodies.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Operator-documented breastfeeding study-pattern boundary (APP B provisional); the second mark requires using the controlled information to rule out the infants' own antibodies, which supports the provisional B.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: low: recorded operator boundary; not proposed for change.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Explain why ready-made antibody protection fades while a vaccinated group responds rapidly later.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The two marks are close to the taught passive-versus-active comparison (antibodies broken down, no memory cells; vaccination makes memory cells), so A is arguable; the scenario does require applying both accounts to two groups, so B is defensible.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium: if the operator treats this as a generic taught comparison like the settled EVAL slots, AO1 would be the better label.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Explain why an outbreak stops in a mostly vaccinated dormitory but continues in a comparable poorly vaccinated one.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The answer largely restates the taught vaccination/transmission account of 3-430 in a named setting (a new setting alone is not B); keeping B is defensible because the learner must attribute the difference between two controlled groups to vaccination coverage.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium: if new-setting restatement of 3-430 is judged reproduction, AO1 would fit.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Decide which of two described leaves (exposed stomata versus stomata in pits retaining humid air) loses water more slowly and why.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The stem supplies the key mechanism (pits retain humid air), so the answer is close to the taught sunken-stomata account (A); the comparison and gradient reasoning about an unnamed structure keeps B defensible.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium: if the pit description is read as simply 'sunken stomata' renamed, AO1 would fit.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Describe the trend in potometer readings at three humidities and convert distances to rates.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: Describing a trend and manipulating data are also B3/B4, but the data are results of the syllabus potometer investigation, so C (interpreting results) is defensible and consistent with 3-393 and 3-454.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: low-medium: if result interpretation without any method or reliability element is to be classed B, AO2 would fit (same applies to 3-393 and 3-454).

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Give the reason for scanning a root section at low power before a detailed drawing.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: This is a taught microscope technique, which the syllabus places under A3 (techniques of operation of apparatus); it is also practical method reasoning for the drawing task, so C is defensible.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium: if A3 technique recall is to be kept separate from C method demands, AO1 would fit.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Make a large, unshaded labelled drawing of a spinal cord transverse section from a photomicrograph, showing the grey matter, white matter and central canal.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The workspace crosswalk counts drawing from a specimen as C, and similar photomicrograph drawings (3-129, 3-130, 3-226, 3-355) are AO3 Apply. One mark here is purely drawing quality. Against that, the approved plan classes this objective as A-taught, and three of the four marks reward a structure layout the learner could reproduce from memory. The heart drawing 3-386 is labelled the same way.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium: I would move it to AO3/Apply if the teacher decides that marks for drawing from an image make it C2 whatever the objective. 3-386 should then be reviewed with it for consistency.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Reason that because anaerobic respiration releases less energy per glucose molecule, a muscle with the same energy demand must break down more glucose per minute.
boundary_cases_kept.reason: The first mark is taught recall (3-025). The second needs a consequential step: if the demand stays fixed and the yield per glucose falls, the rate must rise. That step is modest but it is real reasoning, so B is defensible.
boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium: I would move it to AO1 if the teacher regards 'more glucose is needed' as part of the taught aerobic/anaerobic comparison.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Match two described responses (fast and brief versus blood-borne and lasting hours) to nervous or hormonal control.

boundary_cases_kept.uncertainty: medium: I would move it to AO1 if the teacher sees it as recognising the taught distinction rather than handling information.

boundary_cases_kept.prompt_demand: Decide which culture (bacteria or viruses inside animal cells) a cell-wall-blocking medicine affects, and give the reason.
